messages:
anya: Customer on Dedicated (VPC) started seeing 401s after they enabled the new perimeter LB (HAProxy v2.4) in front of our L7 gateway. They say the browser sends an SSO cookie and LB rewrites it to an Authorization header, but backend Redwood service receives no Authorization header. Repro steps below.

anya: Repro (high-level):
1) Browser -> HAProxy (TLS terminate) sets `Authorization: Bearer <opaque>` from cookie transform
2) HAProxy -> Dedicated gateway (Istio ingress) -> sidecar -> service
3) Service returns 401, logs show no Authorization header present.

anya: Header dump from curl at LB (shows Authorization present):
```
> GET /api/v1/generate
> Host: api.customer.example
> Authorization: Bearer abc.def.ghi
> X-Forwarded-For: 10.0.1.12
```

anya: Header dump from service (via debug endpoint):
```
Received headers:
Host: internal-svc
X-Forwarded-For: 10.0.1.12
Cookie: session=xxxxx
# NO Authorization header here
```

anya: Customer tried adding `http-request set-header Authorization %[req.hdr(X-Forwarded-Authorization)]` on HAProxy and also tried setting `preserve_host`, no dice. Need advice if gateway or Istio is stripping or rewriting.

devon: Thanks, anya. Curious if the Istio ext_authz filter is running and returning a 401 earlier which causes the router to drop headers. Can you grab the envoy access log at the gateway for that request? Look for `-` in the :authority or authorization column. Also confirm if TLS is terminated at HAProxy (it is per your note).

devon: Also, can you confirm whether HAProxy is proxying with PROXY protocol (TCP) or plain HTTP? If PROXY protocol is enabled and the gateway expects plain HTTP, some headers can get mangled.

lee: Two quick checks: 1) Is there any `x-envoy-external-address` / `x-forwarded-proto` mapping that triggers our header normalization? 2) If the LB injects `Authorization` via `http-request set-header`, HAProxy will overwrite an existing header; but it should still be forwarded. Might be an Envoy config on the Dedicated gateway that canonicalizes/blocks `Authorization` unless explicitly allowed.

olivia-support: I opened a customer ticket with priority P1. Customer provided a pcap showing HAProxy sending Authorization to the gateway IP on port 80. I also asked them to enable debug on the gateway pod to capture envoy raw headers.

infra-bot: trace-id=trc_0009a; gateway-ingress-1 -> ext_authz check -> upstream service call -> ext_authz response=allowed; router forwarded to upstream; final upstream response=401. (auto-run tracer)

anya: Attached envoy request-level debug (from pod):
```
[2026-03-15T09:12:23.123Z] "GET /api/v1/generate" 401 - - 0 - - "10.0.1.12" "curl/7.79.1" 0 0 0 - "-" "-" "-"
# There is an ext_authz stage but it returned allowed; still no Authorization field logged.
```

devon: Ok. Two likely roots: (A) HAProxy is using `http-request add-header` style which sets `X-Forwarded-Authorization` and our gateway has a rule to drop `Authorization` unless it originates from edge LB TLS termination where we validate client certs. (B) Istio sidecar or an Envoy http filter earlier is configured to remove `Authorization` for internal requests for security (we did this to avoid leaked bearer tokens across internal mesh). We should look for `token_forwarding` flags in our gateway config under `deployment/dedicated/gateway-config.yaml` (search for `forward-authorization`, `preserve-auth-header`, or `remove-auth-on-internal`).

devon: As a quick workaround for the customer, ask HAProxy to set a custom header like `X-Customer-Auth` instead of `Authorization`, then add a small hook in the gateway config to copy `X-Customer-Auth` -> `Authorization` for requests coming from that LB CIDR. Example HAProxy snippet:
```
http-request set-header X-Customer-Auth %[req.hdr(Cookie),regsub(^.*session=([^;]+).*$,\1,)]
```
And Gateway (envoy lua or ext_authz hook) to copy header if present.

lee: If we do an internal copy in gateway, be careful about token validation path. ext_authz will run before some filters, so if ext_authz expects Authorization it may still fail. Order matters: copy header as early as possible (envoy listener or filter chain). I'll draft a temp Envoy Lua filter we can drop into the listener to copy.

olivia-support: Customer tried the `X-Customer-Auth` approach and PBX shows the gateway now receives `X-Customer-Auth`, but ext_authz still complains `no authorization header`. So we need the copy to happen before ext_authz. Any quick patch?

devon: Can you push this minimal Lua to the gateway (listener filter position 0):
```
-- lua copy header
function envoy_on_request(request_handle)
  local h = request_handle:headers()
  local v = h:get("x-customer-auth")
  if v ~= nil then h:replace("authorization", "Bearer " .. v) end
end
```
This will create Authorization early. It isn't ideal long-term (we must audit) but works as emergency workaround.

anya: I applied the Lua to a staging gateway and customer confirms it fixed the 401s. We need a proper long-term fix in Dedicated: either document allowed header passthrough from known LB CIDRs or add config toggle `preserve_authorization_from_lb` with CIDR whitelist.

lee: Agreed. I'll open an infra PR to add a flag and a test that ensures Authorization is preserved if request originates from a configured external-LB CIDR and TLS was terminated at that LB. Also add a note to Dedicated deploy docs about avoiding TLS re-termination that strips headers.

olivia-support: Closing loop with customer: told them staging fix implemented and we're pushing a config change to prod next week. They asked for a postmortem explaining why Authorization was blocked — can we include the ext_authz/filter-order detail so they understand?

devon: I'll draft the postmortem and include: how HAProxy header transforms, how Envoy/Istio internal policy can remove headers, the Lua temporary mitigation, and the long-term `preserve_authorization_from_lb` toggle + security checklist.

anya: Thanks everyone. Saving artifacts: pcap, envoy debug logs, HAProxy config snippet, staging Lua patch.

olivia-support: Noted — ticket updated, customer happy with mitigation, assigned eng-infra for the PR. :thumbsup:
